text:
maria: Heads-up — hit a weird streaming bug in the sample chat app. Client disconnects + quick reconnects sometimes produce out-of-order chunks in the UI.
kevin: repro steps?
jules: seen this too in prod when a flaky proxy sits between client and our SSE endpoint. Can you paste logs?
maria: minimal repro: open stream, force-close client (network tab), reopen immediately. Server keeps sending chunks but client UI shows chunk N+1 before N.
maria: curl repro: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream?model=chat-lite"
```
then ctrl-c and rerun quickly.
kevin: that sounds like the proxy is buffering partial frames and then flushing them on reconnect. Did you see repeated event ids? logs: 
`[stream] id=42 chunk=1/--`, `[stream] id=42 chunk=2/--`, then after reconnect `id=42 chunk=2` arrives twice.
jules: we also observed token refresh mid-stream causing the client to open a new connection while old in-flight was still finishing; backend then emits remaining chunks on old conn and on resume which can cause dupes or ordering issues.
maria: interesting — in our case token didn't rotate but the ISP dropped TCP socket; the TCP FIN arrived late at the proxy. Proxy then retried and merged buffers.
kevin: possible mitigations: 1) make SSE messages self-contained, include a monotonically increasing seq field in each event so client can reorder/deduplicate. 2) emit an explicit "event: block_end id: <n>" sentinel after each logical block. 3) use Last-Event-ID on reconnect to resume from last seen id.
jules: agree. Also SDK-level: expose an option to enable strict ordering/dedup mode where the SDK buffers small out-of-order chunks and reorders by seq (configurable max-latency e.g., 200ms). That would improve DX without server changes.
maria: is there any standard SSE header we can leverage to detect mid-stream auth expiry? We saw a 401 on reconnect sometimes.
kevin: Last-Event-ID is part of SSE protocol for resuming, but it assumes server retains state. For auth, we could add a short-lived sticky resume token returned in-stream as `resume_token` so client can re-auth with minimal permission and continue. Could be included in initial response JSON.
jules: short-term fix: in the sample app docs add a note to close existing stream before opening a new one, and add jitter/backoff on automatic reconnects. That reduces races.
ops-bot: deploy notice: canary of proxy config rolled out to reduce aggressive keepalive timeouts at 10:12 UTC.
maria: thanks — small follow-ups: (1) can we add seq numbers to the chat-lite model today? (2) SDK patch to expose `max_reorder_ms`?
kevin: I'll open an RFC in git and a tiny PR in the JS/TS SDK for maxReorderMs + dedupe by seq. For server seq numbers, I'll ping infra/product to see if adding id per token is acceptable for hosted.
jules: I'll update the sample-app README with curl repro and recommended client pattern (use AbortController, wait for close, add small backoff on reconnect).
maria: sample message snippet for SDK docs we can use: 
```
// on message
if (message.seq <= lastSeq) return; // dedupe
if (message.seq !== lastSeq + 1) bufferAndReorder(message);
```

kevin: also add metrics: emit a "stream-reorder" counter when reordering/dropping occurs so we can measure incidence.
devex-bot: reminder: thread pinned in #devex until PRs are linked.
maria: cool — thanks all, will paste links once I have the PRs and updated README. :thumbsup:
kevin: great, ty.
jules: fwiw, for long-term we should consider gRPC streams for clients behind weird proxies — less ambiguous framing than SSE.
maria: true but higher barrier for quick-start. Let's start with seq + SDK dedupe first.
kevin: created issue #4123 (internal) to track server seq addition and SDK flags.
maria: linking PRs here when ready.
